metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; correct by adding 2–5% to forecast to account for downward momentum reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overcorrects downward; apply a 3–7 day lagged “overshoot buffer” to avoid premature retracement.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., >0.4) within 3–5 days, model underreacts; increase forecast by 1–3% per sentiment unit shift to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day avg, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true volatility; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or positive, especially near event windows (e.g., policy announcements, auction dates).
- If sentiment history shows repeated “negative → positive” transitions, model tends to lag; apply a 2–4 day delay in adjusting forecast to align with sentiment momentum.
